groups.defect: When buffer.assigned_shards is empty, num_processes becomes min(...,0)=0. No flusher processes or buffers are created, so flushing and the submit() checks (record_stored_segments, backpressure, memory) silently do nothing.

answer.reasoning: All three suggestions point at line 51, but the code has two separate problems there. (1) An explicit max_processes=0 is treated as missing by `or`, so the limit falls back to len(shards). That is all s_975b3a2a reports. (2) An empty shard assignment produces num_processes=min(x,0)=0, so no flusher runs. This happens whatever value max_processes has: the CLI default of 1 still gives min(1,0)=0. So an explicit None check alone does not fix it. s_ca82d915 and s_f884b54a both describe problem 2: zero processes or buffers when the shard list is empty, with submit and flush becoming no-ops. That makes them the same defect at the same place. s_ca82d915 also says '0 treated as falsy', which is s_975b3a2a's defect, so it contains s_975b3a2a plus the separate empty-shard defect. That is a partial overlap, not a duplicate. Grouping all three would also be defensible, because every suggestion proposes the same None-check edit on the same line. That is why decisive is false.
